utterances.text: I just wanted to correct myself. It's my mistake. When I mentioned the case Ovcara 1992, and I talked about the ministry, I'm talking about the Ovcara number 93. Could you please tell us the following: The forms were filled in and 90 per cent of the forms that we received here were filled in in February, 1992 [as interpreted]. Could you please tell me, when did Croatia have its own armed forces? When did it officially get its own armed forces? Again intervention for the transcript. We did not get the page number. It should be February '94 and not February '92.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down, especially because there are so many figures.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: To repeat the question, Mr. Grujic, when were the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia officially formed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not a date that I would be able to recall, but I can say the following: I said when the questionnaire was being drafted the members of the commission, including a representative of the Ministry of Defence, participated in drafting the form, and that was the term or the category devised so that the entire range of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia could be included.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your body, whether it was a commission or an office at the time, did not independently decide on the categories to be included in question 18 of the questionnaire, but these categories were set up by the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just one moment. We need to state things very clearly here. When I spoke about the questionnaire, I said that a working group was formed which included people from criminal -- the investigation field, psychologists, computer specialists, analysts, and members of the commission. The commission numbered 10 people at that time, I think, and it was a cross-section of people from all the ministries that would be relevant in seeking missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I have to interrupt you. My question was very clear: Did your office independently formulate question number 18, or was this question number 18 formulated by the Ministry of Defence? Please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire questionnaire was formulated by this working group, including question 18. So the Ministry of Defence didn't say this must be formulated in these terms. Nobody else did that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go to my previous answer -- question to which you failed to answer. Can you tell me with certainty that all of these formations listed under this question, under a) we have Croatian army, under b) we have reserve force of Croatian army, under c) we have ZNG, under f) we have Home Guard. So can you tell me that all of these forces were the legitimate units or legitimate forces of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So they were the legitimate forces of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you whether they were the legitimate forces in 1994 when these questionnaires were filled in. The questionnaires usually refer to the events back in 1991 and 1992, which is after the armed hostilities ceased. So all of these forces that I just listed to you, back in 1991, were they the legitimate forces of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just put a question to me about the legitimacy of a unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You can just say that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can say that I don't know, and I'm saying that I don't know, but I also have to say that the purpose of this questionnaire is not to establish whether they were legitimate or illegitimate, these units. When we created this questionnaire, we needed to specify the formation to which the person belonged in order to be able to trace them. Even if that unit was illegitimate, we had to know which unit they belonged to in order to be able to trace them.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on. Could we please see Exhibit 545. This is the Vukovar table, the Ovcara table. Let me just find out which tab it is. It's tab 2.7. Can we now please look at page 8. Do you have it, Mr. Grujic, page 8? This is the chart reflecting the facts for Ovcara. You have the B/C/S version. On the screen we have the wrong table. The one on the screen is for Vukovar, and we are interested in the one for Ovcara, which is page 8 of 8 of the English version. Thank you. Mr. Grujic, in the upper left table you have methods of identification. And in it we see that 102 persons were identified via using classic forensic methods, and that 90 persons were identified by means of the DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the information we received from forensic experts.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just before you came to testify, we had Dr. Davor Strinovic testifying here, and he spoke of exhumation procedure, autopsy and identification of mortal remains. He provided different information to us. In his data, as much as -- as many as 93 persons were identified via the DNA analysis. His report and accompanying material were tendered into evidence as Exhibit 451. Dr. Strinovic is a member of the commission, isn't he, the commission which exists in your body.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you then explain this discrepancy, this discrepancy that was presented here to this Trial Chamber by the same body?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can attempt to do that. In relation to these three persons, both classic forensic method was used and the DNA analysis. So initially it was the classic forensic method, and later on, additional DNA analysis was done, and this reflects the difference in approach.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there is a difference in numbers. Statistics is all about numbers. As far as I remember the testimony of Dr. Strinovic - I can't remember the exact page of the transcript - he told us that in all cases the classic forensic method was used, and only in cases where it produced no results did they conduct the DNA analysis, which, in certain number of cases, once again, was not successful.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me please explain this to you. This is very important; we should not ignore this issue. All of the persons were processed using classic forensic methods. Not all of them could be identified via this method, but rather, the DNA analysis, and in those instances we had a special method, and the special method produced a number that I gave here. We have samples taken from all of these persons for the DNA analysis. Later on, we proceeded to analyse collectively all mortal remains, including the remains of these three persons. Therefore, they also have the DNA analysis for these three persons. I'm not denying that 90 [as interpreted] persons were analysed via the DNA method.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not included in your table here. If I were to take these tables, then I would have two different tables with different sets of results. Tell me, are these public records? Could anybody have access to them? Anybody studying this issue, the issue of the number of the exhumed and identified persons from Ovcara or from any other location in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Absolutely. And they were included in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Intervention for the transcript. 49, line 6, it should say 93 persons. Mr. Grujic, comparing various tables we received from you, we established that you had a number of categories when it comes to mortal remains as well as to the persons who were sought, detained, and so on. Only in this table, the one for Ovcara, do I see that in addition to the status listing defenders, civil protection, civilians, and unknown status, you also have something referred to as "special status." Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So no other table has this category, "special status," except for this one in Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, since we see here that 192 persons were identified, if we add up the figures in the table reflecting status, we see there 155 defenders, 15 members of civilian protection, 20 civilians, and two of unknown status, we come to the number of 192 or 200. So these 97 plus 12 means 111 persons. So tell me, please, the special status, what are they? They can't be categorised as unknown, they can't be categorised as civilians or civil protection members, which means that they have to go into the category of defenders.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to add up figures, and I did it quickly. So status has a total of 192 persons. Within them we also have those who had a special status, which is to say that they were 97 wounded; out of them, 12 were members of medical staff, and two were journalists. So a person who is wounded as in in the hospital may not be properly referred as a member of armed forces. So this is why we used this solution, to show that there were persons belonging to these categories as well. This was also done in our questionnaires.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all right. But in that case you created a double status for some persons, so there is some overlap. Somebody can also be a defender and a member of medical staff. Because this number of 111 is included in this number reflecting the general status, if I may call it that.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen, can a journalist be a soldier, a member of armed forces? If you believe so, then all right. Or, if -- can a member of medical staff be also a member of armed forces? Well, if yes, then you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. We shall now proceed with further analysis. So there is some overlap in status here. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists and members of medical staff, as you can see, these categories were divided even in the questionnaire, and when we discussed status, you omitted this part, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, in order to abbreviate this overlap issue and also the numbers that overlap when it comes to status, I am now going to put to you the analysis conducted by all three Defence teams. For my learned friends from the Prosecution and for the Trial Chamber I'm going list numbers. Ovcara 90 -- Ovcara 33, 65 ter numbers 694; Ovcara 48, our 65 ter 697; Ovcara 53, our 65 ter -- I said I wouldn't mention the number. Ovcara 87, we did not receive the 65 ter number because that document was disclosed to us last night. And as Mr. Smith said, this was not on the 65 ter list. Ovcara 114, our 65 ter number 654. Ovcara 117, 65 ter number 780. Ovcara 155, our 65 ter number 786. Ovcara 176, our 65 ter number 782. Mr. Grujic, what would your comment be if I were to tell you that in all of these questionnaires the persons tracing their relatives wrote that their relatives or friends were primarily medical workers in the Vukovar Hospital, and in addition to that, they also stated that they were also members of one of the units listed by you in your questionnaire under number 18? That is to say, in these cases that I just read out to you, regardless of whether there are 10, 12, or just five of them, we have an obvious example where there is an overlap in status. Can you then please tell me whether these tables are accurate and whether the classification of the status of these persons is also accurate, and which status did you emphasise when compiling this; the defenders or the medical staff?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you assuredly that this table is accurate, that it was compiled based on the information in the questionnaires, and that the special status is a subcategory that is within it. We did not conduct any further classification where we would say that out of 97 wounded perhaps there were 80 defenders and 12 civilians. No, we didn't do that. So the special status is a subcategory that speaks for itself. And as you could see in the questionnaire, this is not included in the basic category. This is a subcategory. You are right in everything else you put to me. However, it is a fact that we have three categories in this status; those of defenders, civil protection, and civilians, whereas a subcategory can fall under the first one.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if I were to tell you, Mr. Grujic, that all of these names - I don't know exactly how many I've read out to you - are just a combination of one type of status, that is to say medical staff worker from the special status category, and defenders from the status category. I told you that all of these people were actually defenders. Mr. Smith and the Trial Chamber can verify it based on the exhibits that I just mentioned. And I can list another eight persons for you for whom it was stated that they were members of civilian protection, and simultaneously members of one of the formations included in your questionnaire under number 18. Plus the HOS units which were not listed in your questionnaire. I am now going to give you the numbers for the benefit of the OTP and the Trial Chamber, the numbers of questionnaires where, under "status" we have two categories from your tables. And those are cases Ovcara 28, our 65 ter 650. Ovcara 38, our 65 ter number 694. Ovcara 46, our 65 ter number 778. Ovcara 72, our 65 ter number 24. I don't think, though, that this is the proper number, because normally all of these questionnaires have a three-digit number. This can be verified. Ovcara 91, our 65 ter number 633. Ovcara 145, our 65 ter number 845. Ovcara 194, our 65 ter number 747. There are six or seven there within that number. Can you tell me that in this case where in all questionnaires it is stated that the persons traced were members of civilian protection and simultaneously members of armed forces, there is no overlap of status from your table?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat: In all the questionnaires where the civilian protection status is noted, it's stated in the category of civilian protection. So that is why we have the small number 15 civilian protection while the other numbers that are being cited are under the status of overlapping status belonging to another category, so they are part of a different category.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which other category you're talking about now, but you do admit that in cases where civilian protection is mentioned and any other membership, you declared the person as belonging to the civilian protection regardless of the fact that, for example, Ovcara 91, where the same person was a member of the 204th Vukovar Brigade and that Cyrus Vance was present while he was being taken away.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to say this again: The educational status of the persons involved were what they were. And the questionnaires were what they were. So I had to use the information in the questionnaires in the best possible way. You will allow that the interview form, which has 25 pages, you have 3.000 people filling in those forms, most of those people have less than a full primary school education, there are bound to be mistakes cropping up. But what we can say is that on the basis of the information that was available to us we made the best possible and the most correct version of the reports that we could.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, now you are evidently telling us that you are not ruling out the possibility that the information is not quite correct.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say that the information is not correct. I would not say that at all. We have now gone to completely the other extreme. If we take the status and we count the number, we come to 192 identified persons at Ovcara. And as we said, 155 of them were defenders and 15 civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I must interrupt you. I'm saying -- I'm not saying that the information in the questionnaires is not correct, but it's not correct in your tables because you did not mention all these overlaps in status.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But okay, could you please tell me, if this is not correct, would you be able to show that to me? How many persons from the civilian protection did you find?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have just read that to you, but I will continue. I have more things. I wish I didn't have to do this, but you mentioned that there were 20 civilians. Now I am going to dictate 12 cases of questionnaires indicating that the person sought, besides having the status of civilians, were either members of the regular Croatian army or a member of the reserve forces or regular ZNG or reserve ZNG forces. Ovcara 16, our 65 ter number 730. Ovcara 23, our 65 ter 831. Ovcara 34, our 65 ter 694. Ovcara 37, our 65 ter 675. Ovcara 53, our 65 ter 719. Ovcara 117, our 65 ter 780. Ovcara 119, our 65 ter 657. Ovcara 120, our 65 ter 766. Ovcara 163, our 65 ter 711. Ovcara 166, our 65 ter 761. Ovcara 183, our 65 ter 741. And the last one, Ovcara 196, our 65 ter 709. A total of 12 cases. Can you please tell me how these 12 cases, stating that the persons were both civilians and members of one of the formations you mentioned in the questionnaire under question 18, you categorised and entered into your tables in this report.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the procedure was as follows: Asked to provide the number of civilians, the computer provided the number of civilians. Asked for the number of civilian protection members, the computer came up with the number of civilian protection members. And also the same procedure was used for the defence, because the system to do the computer calculations was set up and calibrated very specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that your software programme selected whether it was going to use option a), f), g) or d) under question 18?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it made the selection according to the question that was asked. If we asked for the number of civilians in the records, we would get the total number of civilians. It's a computer calculation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether if at any point you double-checked manually whether there was an overlap in status?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no need. We didn't think that there was any need to double-check the computer data that we got, especially because we were familiar with some of the names.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Grujic. We are now going to move on. You also provided a special table for the special status. Could you please tell us while you were processing the data relating to Ovcara if you received or asked for any information from Dr. Vesna Bosanac.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not directly from her, no. I again would like to emphasise that the data that I am talking about is exclusively the result of reviewing the documents that I have in my office.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you maybe use data that was requested from the MUP?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean "from the MUP"? I'm going to repeat again how we worked with the MUP: The register of all missing persons that we maintained was sent to the MUP so that they could cross-check their records, and if there was any information they had about the missing person in terms of resolving that particular case of a missing person, only for those purposes, if they had any information.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to move to a new topic, and we are going to speak a little bit about the problems of exhumations that were carried out primarily in the Vukovar region. Today you replied to a question by my colleague, Mr. Vasic, and that this was the case in other locations too, that in order to approach an exhumation it is necessary to have an order by the investigations judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether there was such an order by the investigations judge to embark on exhumations in the case of Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the exhumations at Ovcara were not conducted by the Croatian authorities, the exhumations were organised at the request of the International Criminal Tribunal, and it was done under the auspices of the UN, and Human Rights Physicians conducted these exhumations. We, from Croatia, appeared at those exhumations as observers, observers of the procedures and we did not have the opportunity to create any documents or to participate in that process. There were also observers from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and also from the temporarily occupied territories of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you said the exhumations were organised and conducted by this International Tribunal and that the exhumations and autopsies were carried out in the organisation of Physicians for Human Rights, can you please tell us whether the Croatian government has all the complete results of the exhumations and autopsies carried out in the locality of Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My office does not have all of that information. All we have is the data relating to identification. While parts, or actually documents, relating to autopsies were sent to the Institute for Forensic Medicine and they have those available, but we don't have the actual documents on the exhumations itself -- themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Dr. Strinovic told us that your body, your administration, your office, does not even have detailed information about the autopsies, that they never received those parts relating to the cause of death.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the complete material relating to Ovcara is kept?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I don't even know whether that was ever sent to the government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to look at the tables some more that refer to Ovcara -- or rather, Vukovar. Mr. Grujic, you remember that for the needs of the Slobodan Milosevic case you also prepared a report, and the original report dates from 2002, when it was actually prepared for that case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you just worked on it a little bit more, you updated it with the most recent information now that your administration has at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was updated with new information, basically changing just a few details.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the letter and the list you provided, referring to the case of Slobodan Milosevic, in which you informed the Tribunal that one of the persons who was in the indictment - and this letter is from 1997 or 1998, there is no date on it - that you indicated that one person was found alive, Zarko Vilenica, I am going to mention the name now. Do you remember that particular matter?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You've made it easier for me, because now we don't have to refer to any documents. Zarko Vilenica is still registered as a missing person in your office, or no?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's no longer recorded as a missing person.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Because at the Tribunal his name is officially part of the material, and he's been recorded as a missing person.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please allow me to give an explanation. The questionnaires were sent on the basis of possible candidates who could be in the mass graves at Ovcara in 1995. The list of 262 persons and the amended indictment were made much later. We had this information at that particular time, and we sent all the information together with the files. Once we established that the person in question was alive, of course we immediately notified the International Criminal Tribunal, provided all the information, and we took him off the list of missing persons. So he is not on this particular list of 262 persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In any case, that person is alive.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank God.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We spoke a lot about the Ovcara papers, the questionnaires, and the correctness or accuracy of the information on the basis of the tables or the questionnaires. Did it ever happen in your work that numbers of documents, questionnaires, overlapped, and that you would have different information under the name of the same person, under the same name?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand your question, but if it's what I think, then I will try to answer. At the very beginning, when the campaign was being carried out to gather data about missing persons - and I explained how this was conducted on the territory of the Republic of Croatia and outside of it - it happened that at the same time perhaps the brother in Zagreb and father in Sarajevo would both report that a person was missing. Regardless of the fact that they filled in all the required data, when we were entering the data into the database, we would merge those two dossiers so then it would be possible that there would be two or three missing reports about a particular person, but that would eventually become one file.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct, Mr. Grujic. We have several cases where there are two or three questionnaires reflecting that different family members were trying to trace the missing person. But I'm referring to a different case. For example, Ovcara 106 and Ovcara 107. Ovcara 106 is 65 ter number 735. Why don't you write it down. We have a questionnaire for this person, and also an autopsy record, because we received autopsy records that we are now analysing. Both you and Dr. Strinovic confirmed to us that your office, as an official body of the Republic of Croatia, in fact, does not have in its possession the full amount of autopsy reports for the people found at Ovcara. But now to go back to Ovcara 107 and Ovcara 106. As for Ovcara 107, we have information that this person was exhumed but not identified. We have some sort of an autopsy report as well as the report of Dr. Milewski, and she said for Ovcara 107 that its name was the same as the name of Ovcara 106 person. Can you tell us, are there two persons in this case, or just one?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information available to me, I can tell you that all names from the list provided by us, all of these persons went through the identification process. Even though we do not have autopsy reports and cause of death reports, the autopsies were conducted at the Forensic Institute and all of these persons were identified by name by their family members. All of them were recorded as dead persons and registered as such. So all of these persons were identified, but we can't speak of causes of death because, as you said yourself, and Dr. Strinovic said, we do not have complete documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said to us that your office issued certificates. Do you also issue any kind of documents which pertains to the data that you use? Do you issue any kind of certificates for exhumed persons and those identified in various localities in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we do not have such a standard type of certification, but at the request of a court, we can provide some kind of a certificate stating that a certain person was exhumed anywhere, anywhere in the Republic of Croatia, and that the file number is such and such. So we can provide certain elements that are needed to establish certain rights before courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you can also provide such information at the request of the state, based on which I conclude that at the request of Ovcara 107 case any name issued concerning that person would be the name of Ovcara 106 case.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons under 106 and 107 of this list were identified and recorded as dead. Certificates were issued, death certificates, and as such their relatives could obtain relevant documents in various registry offices. We do not issue certificates concerning this number or that number. We know that if a person was identified, identified by the Forensic Institute, then that information is entered into registry books of dead persons and, based on that, death certificate can be issued, and these are normal death certificates that are issued in case of any death.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now we will turn to other tables. The next table after Ovcara table is about Novo Groblje, new cemetery in Vukovar, Exhibit 545, English page 7 out of 8. It's the same tab number. Mr. Grujic, yesterday you told us that you believed that the new cemetery in Vukovar was created when the sanitisation of the terrain was conducted.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sanitisation is conducted once a conflict ceases anywhere; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You also told us that the persons found in that mass grave were most likely -- this was on page 58, line 14 of yesterday's transcript -- that persons buried in that grave -- or, rather, that's page 9956 of the transcript. That the persons buried there are persons who died as a result of aggression, and then people who died when Vukovar was taken, occupied, and then people who died after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As for the period of time, it was before, during, and after.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that Vukovar fell on the 18th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me what time reference was used for this chart, for this table? You gave us certain temporal references about the creation of that mass grave.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we spoke about when the mass grave was created. But if you ask me from what period of time are the victims -- is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that mass grave we have victims from mid-September onwards. From the period of time after the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mid-September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you are claiming that on the basis of autopsy reports or cause of death reports, or some other information you have for these identified mortal remains, and they were a total of 800 of them; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We should also say from which categories these persons were following the sanitisation, and then everything would be clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't tell me whether you established causes of death in relation to all of these persons, how they were injured.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to identifications and those who were identified and exhumed by us, wherever possible we established the cause of death. If it was impossible, we wrote down that the cause of death was not established. That's what we did in 1998, though. On the other hand, in that grave it was clearly visible that bodies were transported into that grave, persons who were killed and are on the list of those who were killed from October. There was a mass grave at the Sloga stadium, and people were buried there with certain markings, because there was no other place. Two-thirds of that mass grave was exhumed and transported to the new cemetery. And these people are on the list, and in certain cases we were able to establish the cause of death. The second category of people are those who were found by the JNA in mass graves, and I told you 28 in Sajmiste, Trpinjska Cesta so many --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So those are the victims. Also, some victims, for example, died in early November and were buried in the Catholic cemetery. For example, I know the last name of Zadro. This person was transported, moved, and then left as unidentified. So we also have that category. And then we have categories from before. And then there are also categories of those who died at the moment when the army entered Vukovar, and we have documents supporting this from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. These victims are easily recognised - easily recognised - and they are from that period of time. So following the occupation of Vukovar, we also have victims who were prisoners of war. There were 11 of them, and they were from Trpinjska Cesta. They surrendered there. One last name that I can give you from that category is Savoric, and I can remember some other ones perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You say that it's very easy to recognise. If these bodies were indeed transported from various other locations in Vukovar and then finally deposited at the new cemetery in Vukovar, I would like to know about these 800 identified cases and what exactly can you tell us about them? Was the time of death established, cause of death, and how the death came about?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat: We established the cause of death on one hand by our forensic experts after autopsy and identification in 1998. For the majority of such cases we also have dossiers which we received from the military court in Belgrade where, in the dossier, they listed injuries, and in the majority of such cases they also marked violent deaths which came about due to fire-arm wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you have it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You have it in regard to these victims. Do you have it here?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it here. Maybe I have one copy of it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But in relation to each of these victims listed in this table, you can't tell us anything about time of death, manner of death, types of injuries they received and the cause of death?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can. Let me take the dossiers out and then I can do it during the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We don't have the papers that all of us can analyse here.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fully agree with you. But I am referring to the documents which I have in my office. I have these documents, and had anybody asked for them, these documents would have been delivered to you. In addition to that, these documents exist at the court in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you see the progress in time of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am doing my best, I'm abbreviating my questions. I think I need another 10 minutes after the break. We split the questions among us, and the topics, so as to comply with the time you gave us, although it is very difficult, in view of the amount of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, does that give you any reasonable hope?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, so far I have always tried to be as efficient as possible, but I have a serious concern. I believe I won't be able to conclude. You saw that we split the topics. Mr. Vasic mostly covered the detained, and you see what Mrs. Tapuskovic is discussing now. I think we came to really important issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not the causes. Is the answer no or maybe?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I need about an hour and a half to two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid we can't finish. Very well. We will have to have the break now and we will look at the consequences at the end of the evidence today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Judge Thelin is, unfortunately, unable to continue this afternoon, so we will continue the sitting as two, under the Rule, for the last session. Yes, Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I tried, over the break, to cut down the number of questions. I don't know how successful I will be. The material is enormous, the material that all the teams had to cover, and even with the division of topics amongst us we are quite overwhelmed with all the papers. But anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, we're going to come back now to the question of the new cemetery in Vukovar. We would need to establish a few other things there. As can be seen from your table -- and I would like to remind everyone that this is Exhibit 545, and the English page number is 7 out of a total of 8 in that exhibit. What we have is that 937 persons were exhumed, and 800 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 938 were exhumed and 800 identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you said that these bodies were covered by documents which you received from the authorities of Serbia and Montenegro; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please tell us if, according to the documents received from Serbia and Montenegro, were you able, when you examined the documents later, to establish the day of death for which number of cases, and was it possible at all to establish the day or time of death?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents do not give the time of death. What they do give is the time when the mortal remains were found. The date of death can be established on the basis of a number of parameters, such as when something happened which is documented, there are documents to substantiate that, and also on the basis of examining the mortal remains that were found in a certain place.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We've already heard something about these parameters used from Dr. Strinovic too. But as for you, these 800 persons that were identified have no established time of death, as far as you're concerned. To continue then, we have a breakdown, and these 800 mortal remains -- we have a breakdown for these 800 mortal remains, and it is stated whether the death was a violent death, whether it was a gunshot wound as the cause of death, or whether the cause of death was an explosive device.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the exact numbers. This is not exactly in my line of work. This is something that forensic medicine would deal with. But what I saw was that the majority of deaths were caused by violent means and by gunshot wounds, and that there was a considerable number of injuries caused by explosive devices, and this is something that can be seen from the documents received in Belgrade, and then later from the documents that we generated.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But at the moment you don't have these documents, and you cannot give us the -- these figures for the names and the numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did not provide such a list. We're talking about a very large number of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also told us yesterday that it's possible with this graveyard -- or grave, that people were buried there who had died of natural causes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did mention that possibility, and it's possible that a small number of people could be amongst these total number of people who had died of natural causes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this could be death from old age or from illness?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I remember information regarding the oldest person. The oldest person found there was 103 years old.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But if we look at the tables that you gave us, at all the locations, or rather all of the mass graves you also established the average age or the age of the person, as well as their gender. Would you agree with me that all other localities -- at all other localities the number of women is not -- does not exceed 20 per cent, whereas the Vukovar cemetery, the number of women is over 23 per cent. Could you please explain to us why this is so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Would that lead us to the conclusion that women do not participate in such numbers in combat, and that the numbers then here of persons who had died outside of armed conflict is slightly greater?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The percentage of women who died of natural causes is slightly higher here than is usual, as demonstrated in your other tables.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the cause of death, we cannot talk about the cause of death. All we can talk about here is that the percentage of women who died here is higher than at other locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is whether this can lead us to the conclusion that this percentage is higher because you mentioned the possibility that persons were buried in the grave who had died of natural causes, and that would be the reason why the percentage of women is higher.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be hard for me to conclude something like that. The reason probably is that if we're talking about natural causes of death, that these were elderly people who happened to be in their houses and simply died of old age because of poor food, their health was damaged, and so on and so forth. But we could not establish causes of death in such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't have that information, then, do you? All right. Very well. Your information for the new cemetery in Vukovar indicates - and this appears in two tables - that we have a total number of 938 exhumed and 800 identified persons. And I've already said that we have heard here from Mr. Ivan Grujic, who -- excuse me, Dr. Strinovic. Dr. Strinovic, who gave us slightly different data on the new graveyard -- new cemetery in Vukovar. Could you please explain this difference in the figures of the exhumed and identified persons as provided by two persons who work in the same official body of the government of the Republic of Croatia and who are appearing before this Tribunal as court experts -- or as experts.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what other information or different data he could have in relation to the Vukovar cemetery, but perhaps I can explain that, if he did happen to have different information, different data.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I think the information varies in relation to two or five mortal remains. What I'm interested in is, however, how can we have a statistic information drafted by the same body and that the outcome would be different in -- in the final result?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly what the difference is. What are we talking about so that I could then try to clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to say that we're talking about Exhibit 451 now. It's the table attached to Dr. Strinovic's report, which has been tendered here as an exhibit, where it is stated that there were 990 persons. His figure is higher than the figure that you provide.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let us provide an explanation immediately, if you allow me, so as not to waste time. Dr. Strinovic included a figure where he included the Sloga stadium, and I discussed this before. So the location where there were 210 mortal remains, if I'm not mistaken, 140 of whom were taken out by the members of the JNA and moved to the new cemetery, while 70 were left at the Sloga stadium. When we did the exhumations at the new cemetery, the Sloga stadium grave was exhumed as well, so he provided the total figures, because this was done during the same time period and at the same location.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Grujic. I accept when you say that the figure includes the mortal remains from other localities, but this is something that is not evident from the tables, that the tables provide the final figures. At this stage we are operating with the final figures. So we need to know how many were found at which localities, which time period, and so on. We need to have the precise data. Your body has been working on this data for 15 years.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I state that the new cemetery had 938 victims that were exhumed there at the new cemetery. Also, the 70 persons were exhumed at the same time, and that is why Professor Strinovic placed them in the same figure. On the other hand, official statistics are issued by my institute, and his figures come from the Institute for Forensic Medicine.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You have members of your commission and then you engage the staff who are participating in your work. So what I would like to know is do you compare the data? I can give you cases where the data was not compared.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say the following: All institutions, including the Institute for Forensic Medicine, need to send the results they have or the findings they have to our administration. All the information is officially recorded and it becomes part of the official record. So it's possible that some findings are not sent to us because of an administrative mistake. But all the information should be sent to us, we compile it, and this is all then sent from us to the Croatian government, to the relevant bodies, to the international institutions, and also to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So the information that we have analysed so far, and on that basis you drafted the final statistical figures -- we looked at the overlaps in status that were there, but you drafted the official statistics for the government and for the Croatian Assembly after working on all of these cases for 15 years.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you permit, we have indicated the statistical data here, and the data you claim that overlaps, I say it does not overlap. And it was done for the purposes of visually representing the whole event. The official statistics are the tables and we have the basic parameters there.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to move on, Mr. Grujic. We are now going to look at Exhibit 542. That is in the file in front of you, tab 2.11. We're talking about the mortal remains found at -- I'm going to read exactly the heading of that table. List of mortal remains exhumed at Novo Groblje in Vukovar which, according to documents received from Serbia and Montenegro, were found in graves at Velepromet. We're talking about 15 sets of remains; is that correct, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, there was an intervention for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's Exhibit 552.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honours, I apologise. I noted down 542, but yesterday when the numbers were dictated it was a mistake, and I forgot to correct that mistake, so I apologise to all the participants. It is my mistake. It should be 552.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, you have the table in front of you, and it's a list of 15 persons. As you can see the first three persons are unidentified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like for us now to look at person 3, listed here as NN II/186, and an asterisk; is that correct, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There is no other data entered in the table for that person; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the table asterisk denotes that this person, NN II/186 was not accompanied by any documentation, nor were the remains found that could be linked with this reference II/186; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, then, in this case where you don't have a body and you have no documentation, how come you put this person on the list?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to clarify. As you can see, all of the persons on this list were given numbers when they were buried, which means that they comprise a group. The same event, same time of autopsy, and same time of burial. In that group we found this reference that we listed here, which means that there are documents pertaining to that person, but we did not receive them from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and that this person was exhumed before we got to our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I would like to know what parameters you used to link this person NN II/186 with new cemetery in Vukovar and Velepromet? How did you establish the connection?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to explain again. We received from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia a list. First we received a list with all dossiers. In that list there was a dossier NN II/186. When the documentation was turned over to us, this particular dossier was not given to us. That's one thing. On the other thing, when we conducted exhumation at the new cemetery, the mortal remains, both before and after, have their own marks on the body bag. This number was between the two bodies, but there was no body accompanying it. There was just an empty space. So, based on that, we concluded that, yes, there was documentation, and yes, there was a body. Because, had there not been a body, there would have been no documentation, no dossier offered to us in the initial list. That's one thing. The second thing is that all of these persons who are from Velepromet have their ordinal numbers and they were listed under those numbers. So we have a total of three elements based on which we concluded that, yes, this person existed and there were mortal remains. I'm not say that anything bad took place here. Most likely a family member provided us some information.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, when did you receive dossiers from Serbia and Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That process took almost three years.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When did you receive the last dossier or protocol?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From 1998 you did not receive a single piece of information which would in any way provide any kind of parameters for this person NN II/186, especially confirming that this person was exhumed at the new cemetery in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite all of our efforts aimed at receiving not only this document but also documents from the Vukovar Hospital and other places, unfortunately, we did not receive these documents, and there are records to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Together with this table we received another document accompanying it. We received it from the OTP. That's the following page, ERN number 0600-3794. Do you have that page in front of you, Mr. Grujic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us then, can you anything be seen on the note which we see here in this photograph? We see a hand holding a note. Can anything be read from that note?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it. It's not clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell me, in the bottom right corner, in the bottom right corner we have some sort of a stamp, and then above it we have II-181.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We see that the three unidentified persons from the previous list are all marked with NN. So, this marking here, NN 181, can it be linked at all with the three NN persons from the list?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These numbers II/189, II/188, II/186, are numbers of dossiers or protocols we received from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. So that's the main number of the dossier which was found on the cover of the dossier and is then repeated in all of the documents within that dossier.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What about this dossier, NN -- or rather, the one marked with II-181. At the bottom it says "NN, male body." We don't have it on the list. Can we then conclude that II-181 and II-186 have nothing to do with Vukovar and bodies who found there, because it says here that those were plain graves in Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those were not plain graves. These were mass graves. And that can be shown by documents that came later on. The same three mass graves were the ones that were found across from Velepromet, as is stated here. The JNA took out mortal remains from these graves and transferred them to the new cemetery. We have additional four similar documents found on mortal remains which were exhumed and mentioned on the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, my question was very simple. Your table containing this page was exhibited. I asked you whether you can link this number, II-181 with any of the 15 listed persons on the list.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can list -- link it with Senica Boris [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what you think, but can you corroborate it, can confirm that that is that person?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it on me, but I can send you these documents, I can obtain them for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You wrote down that the dates these persons went missing was the 18th of November. 18th, 19th, and 21st of November. Two persons went missing in Borovo Naselje and the rest went missing in Vukovar. We know nothing about these three persons, the first three persons. Do you know for any of these persons the time of their death, the manner and cause of their death?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the document here, but I can tell you, for example, about the person whom I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, we are dealing only with papers here. We can't rely on memories here.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could not have brought my entire records here. I only brought what was necessary, and if you find any other piece of documentation necessary, I am prepared to send it. We have dossiers. All of the numbers you mentioned have corresponding dossiers created by the JNA. We also have our autopsy reports. So the documentation is of a good quality and is quite voluminous.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. But you brought this list, it was tendered into evidence, and you now cannot give us a single relevant piece of information as to the time of death of these persons. You only have the date when they were last seen, the date when they went missing. But you also can't tell us anything about the cause of death or --

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the table here you have the dates when these persons were last seen or when they went missing. One of the dates -- or rather, the dates are 18th, 19th to 21st of November. The fact that they were killed before the 7th of December, 1991, that is the fact. I can't tell you exactly when they were killed, but somewhere between these dates. And we know this on the basis of fact that the mortal remains were found on the 7th of December, and they went missing on the 21st of November, so in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in relation to person II-181, I cannot accept you linking this date, the 7th of December, as the last day they could have been killed, and you linking it with the 15 persons on the list. This person II-181 is not on the list. Did you try to obtain any other information from Serbia and Montenegro in relation to this table?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you in my previous answer that not once but in many contacts that we had, also attended by the representatives of the international organisations working within this field, in these contacts we asked not only for documentation about the new cemetery but also documentation on mass graves in the territory of the Republic of Croatia, victims from those graves, documentation about the mass graves that were relocated in the territory of Croatia, especially in the Podunavlje region. Those were our basic requests in our contacts with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That was all properly recorded in minutes from these meetings and verified by international monitors. In addition to that, we also asked for documentation from the Vukovar Hospital which had been taken away. These are all the documents that we requested but never received. What I presented here was based on what we did receive.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now going to use this opportunity, Your Honours, to introduce here a questionnaire that we just received yesterday. It was not exhibited and it doesn't have a 65 ter number because it wasn't on the list. However, we received it last night from the OTP; it's in the system. Could we please put it on the screen. 0102-4237 to 4250. Your Honours, we wonder whether this document has been put into the system since last night. If not, I have a hard copy here, and I can give it to the witness now. Could the usher please assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, that document is not in the system. These are the 15 I was referring to this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be placed on the ELMO, but we do not want to display the name, Your Honours. Could the name be protected, please. We will try not to mention it, but to mention it as little as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the questionnaire?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please turn to the last page of this questionnaire. And we can see here that it was possible to enclose various documents with the questionnaire. This is the last document. We don't have the translation, but can you please read it out, sir, without mentioning the name. This is a very brief letter. It was sent by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read this out?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Dear sir, We are pleased to inform you that Ribicic Marko, the person you were tracing, has been found. He was registered by the ICRC on the 28th of December, 1991, at the camp in Nis. If you wish to send a message, we are enclosing a form for writing a message which you may send to the following address."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be tendered into evidence, Your Honours? And we will put it in the system when possible. It is clear why we haven't been able to do it so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. And the name is not protected, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour. Just out of respect for the victims and their families, I tried that the name not be mentioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document will become Exhibit 556.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, can you tell me, once you receive such information, what steps do you undertake?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the only such document or notification that we received in different ways indicating that a person being traced was alive. In such cases at the first upcoming negotiations or talks we tried to establish that it really is so. And then if we do prove that, and secure agreement from the other side that the person is alive, then we embark on negotiations for their release. Unfortunately - and I say unfortunately - this is probably some sort of substitute identity, because a person that was born on the 11th of November, 1951, is called Marko Ribicic, and I'm going to say that publicly precisely because the information that can be then understood can reach their family and can cause suffering again. That person, unfortunately, was found and identified on the 5th of February, 1998. They were exhumed from the Ovcara mass grave. And I'm very sorry that that document was not actually true.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We have another case, it's Ovcara number 78. In your list you can find out who that is about. From the questionnaire, and the Trial Chamber and my learned friends can see, that the seeker attached with the interview form with the questionnaire a tape recorder, audio tape. Audio tape that was recorded in January, 1992, at a hospital in Nis where the person being traced was together at the hospital with the person who had the -- made the audio tape and gave it to the person's brother. Could you please tell us whether you submitted that audio tape to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. I don't know if that tape is still amongst our documents or whether it was returned to the person seeking the person. But if you allow me to say something very briefly. In a series of situations, unfortunately, we did encounter such evidence that somebody was alive somewhere. But what usually happened in practically all of the cases, in fact, and that was later proved, that it was a question of providing the relatives false hope that somebody was still alive, exclusively for the purposes of material gain. So the relatives would actually pay for such audio tapes, they would pay a lot of money for that. I can recall the number of the son of Mrs. Oliveric [phoen] who was alive and he was in the JNA, and she happened to pay 5.000 euros for such a tape. Unfortunately, these are situations where people in bad faith try to gain material profit from such cases, but usually the case is that that person was already dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell me whether there is the possibility -- would you be able to confirm that in none of the remaining cases we cannot say -- or rather, in the rest of the cases we cannot say that there has been no misuse in using the data? Can you guarantee the accuracy of the data in all the questionnaires?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. As I said, this is information provided by the relatives for the exclusive purpose of tracing the person. It's in the interest of the family for us to find the person that is being sought.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I am now going to move to my last group of questions, and that relates to persons on the indictment, and who, according to your information -- or actually whose mortal remains were found in different places. Could you please tell me, for example, we are talking about the mortal remains marked - and probably that is your marking - 1.105, and these are ERN number 0100-6299. It's information referring to a person, a gentleman born in 1915, and in your documents it says that he was treated in Novi Sad. What can you tell us? How did he get included on the list of persons allegedly missing from the hospital when it says that he was transferred to the Novi Sad hospital much earlier and before the JNA units arrived at the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when he was transferred to Novi Sad. I don't have official information about that. It's not a question. If we're talking about the same person, that person is not born in 1915. We would have to correct that.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It is correct. I'm going to tell you his name now. The date of birth of the person in question is the 1st of June, 1915. This is 65 ter number 715. Mr. Grujic, I asked you whether you requested or received any information from Vesna Bosanac, and you denied receiving any kind of information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not receive any information from Mrs. Vesna Bosanac.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, what were the criteria under which these questionnaires were presented to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anywhere where the Vukovar Hospital was mentioned. And that was a broader analysis because we couldn't know and did not know who the people were who were in the hospital. All we could do was to make an analysis, and I said that for precisely those reasons we researched -- actually, we requested documents from the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia so that we could establish that. And all the documents that were presented to the Tribunal were drafted on the basis of a possible reconstruction, and the success of the reconstruction is indicated by the number that, out of 264 people, 192 have already been identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going refer, for the benefit of my learned friends and for the Trial Chamber, to a number which does not have an Ovcara number because the person is still being registered as a missing person. This is 65 ter number 686. Now I'm going to read, and my colleagues will be able to check, that in that case the Vukovar Hospital is not mentioned once and that the person was last seen near the building of the former Territorial Defence, near the house with the basement. Then do you have an explanation of how this particular case came to the Tribunal if you were asked to deliver all the cases that were related to the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our records were available to the investigators, and on the basis of their own information and experience they decided what documents would be copied and sent to the OTP. This is one thing. Secondly, and when you mentioned this, and I can clarify that, you said that the gentleman was taken to Novi Sad for treatment, and that you have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we carried out an exhumation together with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia of all the unidentified persons being sought by the Republic of Croatia. This did take place in Novi Sad, and we did not find the person that you are talking about. So something is not quite right in the assertions made by your investigators, you are talking about investigators. So this has not been proved in Novi Sad to date. All the exhumations were carried out in Novi Sad, DNA samples were taken, and such an identity has not been confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What I can say to you now is -- all right, very well. Obviously the investigator did not provide accurate data, and this is what we were talking about, how much the information was verified, and that was your duty in accordance with the laws in accordance with which you were established. All I want to say is that among these 60 persons that were not found that are still being considered as missing, I'm going to name another few cases where we again -- where it is not mentioned in any way -- where the hospital is not mentioned in any way as the place where the traced person is -- was seen for the last time. For example, we are talking about document, for the benefit of my learned friends and the Trial Chamber, 65 ter 680. There is no Ovcara number because the person is still being registered as a missing person. We're also -- have the example of two more persons. One of them is 65 ter 803, and another person, 65 ter number 622 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just briefly object to that question. The witness has answered this question in a way in relation to another case, stating that in situations where in the missing person's report the Ovcara hospital [sic] was not stated, the investigators from the Tribunal may have had other criteria to select that documentation, so it would be simply be a repeat of the same answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not a basis for objection, Mr. Smith. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, for interrupting you. Intervention in the transcript: Page 85, line 6. Instead of "investigators," the B/C/S term used was "trazitelj," "trazitelj."

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We now talked about the persons whose mortal remains were not found, who were not identified, and we said that they are in no way connected to the hospital, which was one of the criteria to present the material. The Ovcara-related cases, and I'm interested in your comments, we checked and saw that at least 20 cases - and now I don't have time to give you all the names - are also the persons that are in no way connected to the hospital. My question is: Is there any other external factor that influenced you and made you send these documents to The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must repeat, and I will repeat, that we sent all the cases requested. There was a much broader list which was the element on the basis of which the investigators requested the documents to be sent, and they provided a list of the people they wanted the documents on. And this is what we did. That doesn't mean that the hospital needed to be mentioned in the questionnaire. If you permit me, it does not mean -- there are other people who were identified and the hospital is not mentioned in their questionnaires either. And also, if you permit me, you said something to which I must react. I must ask, actually, for your advice. You said that we never verified for so many years where all these people disappeared to. What I would like to know is what would be the mechanism, the way and the possibility for us to be able to do that. This is the only source of information that we were able to obtain.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Grujic, I did not make that comment, and I take into account what you are saying. I am aware of your position, your function. All I said was that in 15 years, cross-checking of information was not carried out. Also I would like to say that the information that we had for which I don't have time for but the colleagues from the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber, when they review that, will see that in a large number of cases these questionnaires do not state that the persons being sought were injured or wounded in any way. Still, I only have one more question for you, sir. Since you were in the function that you were in, was there any possibility for a certain person to receive posthumously a rank or some form of recognition for having participated in the armed forces in any of the units that were mentioned in question 18 of your questionnaire, although they, in actuality, had nothing to do with the armed forces during the relevant time period? Do you know of any such cases?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know who received which benefits or did not receive certain benefits by name, first and last name. It's something that I really cannot tell you anything about.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether any benefits were secured and you did not maintain such records?

utterances.speaker: IVAN GRUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one intervention to the transcript. This is page 85, line 23. It should be 65 ter number 802, and not 622. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I'm afraid, Mr. Lukic, we're going to have to put off your cross-examination. Unless you think you can manage in one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing that makes me happy now is that I'm not beginning my cross-examination now. I would like to do it all in one sitting, so to speak, rather than have interruptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry that it will be necessary for you to return. Arrangements will have to be made by the Office of the Prosecutor for that to occur. And of course the time within which it is to occur is now very limited. We've really only got some two weeks remaining. So we leave it in your hands, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The plan was that the witness would come back on the 12th and testify first thing on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Excellent. But we're just not in a position to allow this Prosecution case to keep just stretching out. So attention is going to have to be paid very closely in the limited time remaining to keeping the examination of witnesses down to what is really important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We understand that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We resume on Monday at 12.30 -- Tuesday. Let me put it with the switch on: Tuesday, not Monday.
